values.note: $15/night for a single unit, no more than 10 people per site; pay at the self-serve fee station. Fees are charged even when the water is off.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/helena-lewisclark/recreation/dry-wolf-campground ('Single Site: $15 per night', '$15/night for single unit. No more than 10 people per site.', 'Please pay at the self-serve campground fee station', 'Even if water is unavailable, campground fees are still required'; page last updated October 13, 2026), read 2026-10-22

values.note: 'All campgrounds on the Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest are first-come, first-served. Reservations are not available.' A site cannot be held by paying for it; the camper must be present. 16 consecutive days in one location.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/helena-lewisclark/recreation/dry-wolf-campground ('Reservations are not available. Camping is limited to 16 consecutive days in one location ... Campsites cannot be reserved by simply paying for the site; camper must be present.'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: 'Dry Wolf Campground is usually open from June through the middle of fall.' Open and close dates vary with snowfall.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/helena-lewisclark/recreation/dry-wolf-campground ('Dry Wolf Campground is usually open from June through the middle of fall', 'Open and close dates can vary depending on snowfall conditions'), read 2026-10-22

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/helena-lewisclark/recreation/dry-wolf-campground ('Dry Wolf Campground's 25 campsites are along Dry Wolf Creek ... The largest slot can accommodate a maximum trailer length of 45 feet.'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: FS lists potable water at this site in the warmer months, but its Current Conditions (page updated October 13, 2026) say 'No potable water available. Fees still required.' Each site has a fire ring and/or grill and a picnic table.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/helena-lewisclark/recreation/dry-wolf-campground (Restrooms 'Vault toilet(s)'; Water 'Potable water is available at this site.'; Current Conditions 'No potable water available. Fees still required.'), read 2026-10-22

note: Helena-Lewis and Clark NF campground along Dry Wolf Creek in the Little Belt Mountains SW of Stanford, below Bandbox Mountain; two fishing platforms on the creek. Access is about 21 miles from Stanford, all but the first mile gravel and dirt and the last 8 miles single-lane. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on the FS page: $15 (page updated Oct 2026), FCFS only (no reservations), 16-day limit, 25 sites, largest slot 45 ft. Added vault toilets, season (usually June to mid-fall), and the current no-water condition (facilities note). Not stated: hookups, senior/access discount. No current alert names Dry Wolf. Note trimmed of restated values; added the single-lane road caveat.
